I found relevant reports; now I'll open the top sources to verify the details.
`torch.OutOfMemoryError` in eval-only is a known `Trainer` pattern:

* **Logit accumulation:** During evaluation, `Trainer` runs forward on every batch and concatenates logits into a single GPU tensor. It moves them to CPU only after the full eval dataset is processed.

> Training fits because it only holds one batch of activations at a time.

* **Default behavior:** By default `Trainer` accumulated all predictions before sending them to CPU, requiring `eval_accumulation_steps` set to a small value to trigger periodic copy.

Fixes documented:

1. `eval_accumulation_steps=16` to offload predictions GPU -> CPU every `n` batches.
2. `preprocess_logits_for_metrics`: run e.g. `argmax` per-batch on GPU before accumulation to store smaller tensor.
3. Reduce `per_device_eval_batch_size`, e.g. to `1`.

Eval OOM is common because eval needs a training batch plus additional space for evaluation.

action.query: Hugging Face Trainer out of memory during evaluation not training

text:
I'll search the web for documented causes of Trainer OOM errors that strike only during evaluation.
The initial results point to likely causes. I'll open the detailed pages to gather citable specifics.
Eval-only `torch.OutOfMemoryError` is a known `Trainer` behavior:

* **Documented cause: logit accumulation:** During evaluation, `Trainer` runs forward on every batch and concatenates logits into a single GPU tensor, moving it to CPU only after the full eval set is processed.
* **Why training survives:** The same setup can train fine because training only holds one batch of activations at a time, while accumulated eval logits grow with eval-set size, model/vocab size, and sequence length.
* Concrete example: keeping full `float32` logits for 2,000 x 512-token sequences with 32k vocab needs ~131 GB; by default those tensors stay on device until the loop ends, so eval dies on the last batch.

Documented fixes:

1. `eval_accumulation_steps`: offload accumulated predictions GPU→CPU every *n* batches; lower uses less GPU memory at cost of more transfers.
2. `preprocess_logits_for_metrics(logits, labels)`: runs per eval batch before caching, e.g. replace logits with `argmax(-1)`, giving `eval_accumulation_steps` a much smaller tensor to hold/offload.
3. Hugging Face forum answer for “CUDA out of memory during evaluation but training is fine”: set `eval_accumulation_steps` to a small value, e.g. 10–20, instead of accumulating all predictions before sending to CPU.

annotations.title: HuggingFace Trainer, in depth: custom losses, num_items_in_batch and gradient accumulation, collators, column pruning and memory-safe evaluation
Cuda out of memory during evaluation but training is fine

text:
Only in `eval` OOM with Hugging Face `Trainer` is a known pattern. Training uses gradients, but it also uses:

* small train micro-batch + `gradient_accumulation_steps`
* train truncation / short `max_length`
* optimizer sharding / checkpointing

Evaluation can undo all of that at once:

### 1. `per_device_eval_batch_size` is too large

`Trainer` has separate batch sizes for train and eval. If you only tuned `per_device_train_batch_size=1-2` to fit, the eval loader can still default to `8` and OOM on the first eval loop.

Fix:

```python
TrainingArguments(
  per_device_train_batch_size=2,
  per_device_eval_batch_size=1, # start here
  eval_accumulation_steps=1, # don't keep all logits in GPU/CPU at once
  eval_strategy="steps",
)
```

This is documented in `TrainingArguments`: `per_device_eval_batch_size` and `eval_accumulation_steps` control eval memory by moving / gathering predictions incrementally [1].

### 2. Eval sees longer / more padded sequences

Eval often uses full documents, `max_source_length` for validation split, or `padding="longest"` in the batch. Without gradients, a single `512-2048+` token batch with `output_attentions=True` or `output_hidden_states=True` can still OOM where short truncated train batches passed.

Fix: use same truncation for eval, set `dataloader_pin_memory=False`, try `group_by_length=True` for eval.

### 3. `predict_with_generate=True` for Seq2Seq / LLM

For T5, BART, Whisper, LLaMA generation, eval doesn't just do a forward pass - it autoregressively generates with KV-cache, `num_beams`, `max_length/max_new_tokens`. That was reported as CUDA OOM only during eval/generation even when training fits [2][3].

Fix:

```python
TrainingArguments(
  predict_with_generate=False, # test if this is the cause
  generation_max_length=64,
  generation_num_beams=1,
)
```

or override `model.generation_config`.

> Rule of thumb: if `train` fits but `eval` OOMs, first set `per_device_eval_batch_size=1`, `eval_accumulation_steps=1`, `predict_with_generate=False`. If eval passes, increase them one at a time.

Sources:
[1] Hugging Face Transformers Trainer `TrainingArguments` docs - `per_device_eval_batch_size`, `eval_accumulation_steps` - https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/main_classes/trainer
[2] huggingface/transformers GitHub Issue - CUDA OOM during evaluation/generation but not training - https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/17994
[3] Hugging Face Forum discussion - Out of memory during evaluation with `predict_with_generate` - https://discuss.huggingface.co/t/cuda-out-of-memory-during-evaluation/17876
